summary: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Phramaha Somboon Watana completed a PhD in 1999 at Panjab University, where Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma were doctoral supervisors (attested 2003).

Phramonchai Saitanaporn works in Buddhist studies. He pursued a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, with committee member Jeff Wilson, and also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Phuntshok Tashi earned a BA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is an indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Radcliffe College and Harvard (PhD ~1969–1973), she held professorships at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (~2004–2020), among other posts.

Pierce Salguero works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (~2005–2010), he held posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010) and the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012).

Pierre Amédée Jaubert was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1796–1798). He served as president of the Société Asiatique (1834–1847) and held posts at the Collège de France and his alma mater.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen specializes in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD in 1991 at Leiden University, where he later held a post as a research fellow (attested 1996).
Pieter Hendrik Pott was a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.
Pietro Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia (~1869–1873). He later held a position at the University of Pavia (~1881–1888).

Piotr Balcerowicz is an indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, the University of Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences (habilitation 2005), and served as deputy editor-in-chief at the University of Warsaw (~1999–2005).

Piotr Klafkowski was a Tibetologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University under Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and traditional teacher Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.
Poerbatjaraka worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1921–1926) and held a post at the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964).

Poh Beng Tan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam. He also studied under teachers Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She was educated at Ohio University (~1967–1969), Goddard College (~1969–1971), and Washington University in St. Louis (~1974–1980).
Pori Park works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Having studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr., she served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.
Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and the University of Calcutta, where he served as a professor (attested 2009).

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Krishnagar Government College and under Sylvain Lévi at the University of Paris, he held posts at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in history and archaeology and Indology. Educated at Vidyasagar College, Presidency University, and the University of Edinburgh (~1882–1888), he held posts at Presidency University (1911–1916) and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture (1916–1936).

Prahlad Pradhan was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Visva-Bharati University and Patna University. His career included posts at Ravenshaw College, Utkal University (~1960–1975), Gangadhar Meher University, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit University.
